- problem: every array of the one library is a `PrimitiveArray` or `PrimImmutableArray` whose 7 bindings named glue classes, so a compiled program would raise at its first array (`explorations/reviews/natives-remainder-2026-11-07.md:34`, finding 1; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:12-50` at 157323e5)
- spec: `Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:68-75` ("Programming Discipline": updates of shared array elements inside `atomic`) and `:133-141` ("Providing the Appearance of a Single Object": a subscript preserves the atomicity of the underlying store)
- precedent: P-164's Java-backed trait with walk's native object below it and the walk-world table entry, `JavaBufferedWriter` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1948-1956`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:798-799`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/JavaBufferedWriterObject.java:23-80`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:493`); P-167's loader device (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:47-53`); `__DefaultVector`'s store in a field (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2672`)
- deviation: walk's loader answers `arrayOps` by one rule onto one new glue class, `ArrayOps`, not onto the three old glue classes, which stay unused (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:181-188,220`); `PrimImmutableRR64Array` joins `NativeArray`'s api (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fsi:18`); `StringPrim`'s program arguments are filled through the array's own `init` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/StringPrim.java:136-139`), a file beyond those named
- historical: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/StringPrim.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java` (each carries the team's copyright header; the clone is shallow, so `a874948ac` is not in it)

The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` from `/home/user/fortress-base28` (exit 0, 4 s). Commits on `wip/rung-array-store`: `6ea756e7` (the walk tests, first) and `fe19fdad` (the edit, its unit test and the refusal test). Every result below ran on the code of `fe19fdad`; no code changed after it.

## What changed and why

P-169 has the arrays' 7 bindings name compiled helpers that walk's loader answers with walk's own operations, and Q2's answer gives the compiled store shape (ii), an `Object[]` with a slot API in the compiled transaction.

- **The store traits** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2391-2406`, api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1610-1627`): `trait JavaArrayStore excludes { String, Number, Boolean, Char, JavaBufferedReader, JavaBufferedWriter }` with `get(i: ZZ32): Any`, `put(i: ZZ32, v: Any): ()` and `init(i: ZZ32, v: Any): Boolean`, bound to `arrayOps.get`, `put` and `init`; `trait JavaRR64ArrayStore`, which also excludes `JavaArrayStore`, with `get(i: ZZ32): RR64` and `init(i: ZZ32, v: RR64): Boolean`, bound to `arrayOps.getRR64` and `initRR64`; the factories `makeJavaArrayStore(n: ZZ32)` and `makeJavaRR64ArrayStore(n: ZZ32)`, bound to `arrayOps.make` and `makeRR64`. They sit right before `primitiveArray` and `__parr`.
- **`NativeArray`** (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:12-46`) is a plain component. `PrimitiveArray[\T, nat s0\]()` holds `mem: JavaArrayStore = makeJavaArrayStore(s0)`, `get(i) = cast[\T\](mem.get(i))`, `put(i, v) = mem.put(i, v)`, `init00(i, v) = mem.init(i, v)`; `PrimImmutableArray` the same without `put`; `PrimImmutableRR64Array[\nat s0\]()` holds a `JavaRR64ArrayStore` and reads `mem.get(i)`. Their `opr [ ]`, `init0` and the team's comment on a failed transaction stay. The api (`NativeArray.fsi`) before: `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray`, each `object ... end`; after: the same two and `object PrimImmutableRR64Array[\nat s0\]() extends ImmutableArray1[\RR64,0,s0\] end` (`:18`), so a program can make it through its own constructor; no factory chooses it (decision A).
- **Walk's native objects** (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:53-59`, right after `trait Object`'s end): `private object JavaArrayStoreObject extends JavaArrayStore end` and `private object JavaRR64ArrayStoreObject extends JavaRR64ArrayStore end`. Their native constructors (`interpreter/glue/prim/JavaArrayStoreObject.java`, `JavaRR64ArrayStoreObject.java`, new) register themselves as `JavaBufferedWriterObject` does; a store's walk value is an `AtomicArray` made with the constructor, as `PrimitiveArray.java:34-35` made one, and an RR64 store's a `double[]`, as `PrimImmutableRR64Array.java:39-46` held one.
- **Walk's loader** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:181-188`, `:220`): after P-167's table, a string that starts `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.arrayOps.` becomes `com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.ArrayOps$` and the method's name, and loads as a glue class does; a name with no operation is refused at load as a missing glue class is. `interpreter/glue/prim/ArrayOps.java` (new) holds `make`, `get`, `put`, `init`, `makeRR64`, `getRR64` and `initRR64`: `get`, `put` and `init` are the bodies of `PrimitiveArray$get`, `$put` and `$init0`, and `getRR64` and `initRR64` those of `PrimImmutableRR64Array$get` and `$init0`, over the two new values. So walk's arrays keep `AtomicArray` and its transactions.
- **The compiled helpers** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/arrayOps.java`, new): `FortressArrayStore make(int)`, `Object get(FortressArrayStore, int)`, `void put(FortressArrayStore, int, Object)`, `boolean init(FortressArrayStore, int, Object)`, `FortressRR64ArrayStore makeRR64(int)`, `double getRR64(FortressRR64ArrayStore, int)`, `boolean initRR64(FortressRR64ArrayStore, int, double)`. Every type maps in the walk-world table.
- **The compiled stores** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FortressArrayStore.java`, `FortressRR64ArrayStore.java`, new). `FortressArrayStore` holds an `Object[]`. Inside a compiled transaction (`BaseTask.getCurrentTransaction()` on a `FortressTaskRunner`), `get` is `TXReadSlot`, `put` is `TXWriteSlot`, and `init` reads the slot and writes it only where it holds nothing; outside one, `get` and `put` are a volatile read and write by a `VarHandle` and `init` a compare-and-set from null. A read of an element that holds nothing raises `IllegalStateException` with walk's message; an index is checked before a write is buffered (`:40-43`). `FortressRR64ArrayStore` holds a `double[]`, takes no part in a transaction, and its `init` writes and answers true, as walk's glue does.
- **The compiled transaction** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java`): a location is a cell (`MutableFValue`) or a `Slot`, an array and an index with identity equality (`:25-62`); the read and write sets are keyed by `Object` (`:78-79`); `committedValue` and `commitValue` read and write either kind, a slot by `getVolatile` and `setVolatile` (`:64-74`); `TXRead` and the new `TXReadSlot` share `TXReadLocation` (`:203-231`), which does not record a location that holds nothing (Hashtable refuses null); `TXWriteSlot` (`:292-297`); both validations and both branches of `TXCommit` read and write through the two helpers. 99 changed lines by `git diff 157323e5 -- ...Transaction.java | grep -c '^[-+][^-+]'`; `BaseTask` unchanged.
- **The checker's walk-world table** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:494-495`): `FortressArrayStore` to `JavaArrayStore`, `FortressRR64ArrayStore` to `JavaRR64ArrayStore`, with the comment above the table naming them.
- **The program's arguments** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/StringPrim.java:136-139`): `GetProgramArgs` cast the varargs factory's result to the old glue's `PrimImmutableArrayObject` (`StringPrim.java:135-141` at 157323e5), which no longer exists for a plain object, so `System` would have stopped as it loads; it now fills the array through `IndexedArrayWrapper`, the array's own `init`, as walk fills a varargs array (`interpreter/evaluator/values/NonPrimitive.java:243-247`).

The bindings, by the record's count (comments and `(*)` lines struck, strings kept): 341 helpers and 102 glue of 443 at 157323e5; 348 and 95 of 443 at `fe19fdad`.

## The measure, the stages and the ladder

The quick pair once on my tree, after the last change of code (`explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh tmp/rung-array-store/mg rung-array-store`, 03:22:20 to 03:23:08 UTC; nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz, 2100 MHz, load 1.60 at the start, JDK 25.0.4.1, FORTRESS_THREADS=1):

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`'s B.11 (the runtime) and B.12 (the natives) place the change: the one library's bindings, walk's loader (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java`), the helpers of `nativeHelpers/` and the compiled run time (`runtimeSystem/`). The library's own way for a type that both paths name and that holds a Java value is P-164's: a trait of `FortressLibrary`, a private native object below it in `FortressBuiltin`, and a walk-world table entry. Sites of that precedent today: one native object below a library trait in `FortressBuiltin.fss` (`JavaBufferedWriterObject`, `:798`), two class entries in the walk-world table (`NamingCzar.java:492-493`), and two names in P-167's table (`NativeApp.java:49-52`). A store in a field is the library's own: `__DefaultVector`'s `mem` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2672`) and `Array2`'s and `Array3`'s. The read at `T` follows the library's `cast` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-36`), as `List`'s `ArrayList` already reads its store (`Library/List.fss:313`).

The ways the language and the library offer, and the choice: the store as a generic trait (the checker refuses a read at `T` against the helper's `Object`, `NamingCzar.java:487`; fork A2); one trait for both stores (a `double[]` class cannot implement it at `Any`); a checker rule for a binding at a type parameter instead of `cast` (fork A3, not taken); walk carrying the store as an `Object` (the review's way (c), which takes walk's writes out of walk's transactions); a cell per element (shape (i), Q2's way not taken).

## What the specification settles

The specification asks that updates of shared elements be made inside `atomic` and that a subscript keep the atomicity of the store (`Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:68-75`, `:133-141`); both stores keep it, walk's by `AtomicArray`, the compiled by the slot keys. The library chapter, typeset from the api, says a re-initialization signals an error (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1510-1515`); neither store signals one (row 466). It asks `i IN bounds()` of a subscript (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1395`) and says nothing of what a subscript out of bounds does.

## Decisions

1. **Shape (ii), one set for both kinds of location.** The read and write sets are keyed by `Object`, a cell or a `Slot`, as the planner's measured model shares them (PROBES.md, probe 1); not separate slot sets, which cost 250 to 550 ns a transaction in the model.
2. **Outside a transaction an element is read and written volatile**, the cell's memory semantics (`MutableFValue.java:18`); not plain, which probe 1 measured at 17.8 ns against 24.1 ns a read and write.
3. **`init` inside a transaction is a transactional read and write; outside one a compare-and-set from null.** So an aborted attempt's initialisation is not kept, as walk's `AtomicArray.init` goes through `ReferenceCell.assignValue` (`interpreter/env/ReferenceCell.java:206-209`); the test checks it. Not taken: a compare-and-set always, which keeps an aborted attempt's value.

# Rung A of climb batch 28: the record lines

## Findings

1. **The one library's arrays hold their elements in a Java-backed store in a field, on both paths.** Holds on `fe19fdad`. `NativeArray` is a plain component (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:12-46`): `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` hold `mem: JavaArrayStore = makeJavaArrayStore(s0)` and read `cast[\T\](mem.get(i))`; `PrimImmutableRR64Array` holds a `JavaRR64ArrayStore`. The two traits and their factories are `FortressLibrary`'s (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2391-2406`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1610-1627`), their 7 bindings on `nativeHelpers/arrayOps`, whose compiled classes `FortressArrayStore` (an `Object[]`) and `FortressRR64ArrayStore` (a `double[]`) the walk-world table reads as the two traits (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:494-495`). Evidence: `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=ArrayStoreJUTest`, 'Tests run: 6, Failures: 0, Errors: 0'; `tests/ArrayStoreWalk`, `ArrayStoreRR64Walk`, through `harness-one.sh`, 'OK (5 tests)' with the team's two native array tests; the count stage 0 and the distance stage 0, `NativeArray` clean in every stage. Meaning: the 7 bindings of `NativeArray` leave glue; 348 of the one library's 443 bindings name a helper and 95 a glue class on this branch (341 and 102 at 157323e5), by the record's count.
2. **Walk answers every name of `nativeHelpers.arrayOps` by one rule with the operation of the same name of the glue class `ArrayOps`, over `FortressBuiltin`'s private `JavaArrayStoreObject`, an `AtomicArray`, and `JavaRR64ArrayStoreObject`, a `double[]`.** Holds on `fe19fdad` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:181-188`, `:220`; `interpreter/glue/prim/ArrayOps.java`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:53-59`). A name with no operation is refused at load: `tests/ArrayOpsMisspeltWalk` with its `.test`, 'OK Saw expected refusal at load', 'Native class com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.ArrayOps$makeStore not found.' Meaning: walk's arrays keep their stores and their transactions; `ant testSystem`, 782 tests, 0 failures; the four-thread runs of `ArrayStoreWalk`'s atomic updates are exact.
3. **The compiled transaction tracks an array element by its array and its index.** Holds on `fe19fdad` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:25-79`, `:203-231`, `:292-297`): a location is a cell or a `Slot`; the read and write sets, both validations and both branches of the commit take either; an element is read and written by a volatile `VarHandle`. Evidence: `ArrayStoreJUTest`, four tasks on a pool of four threads adding 2,000 times each into one element inside the compiled atomic protocol, total 8,000, and a scratch store that bypasses the transaction fails it ('expected:<8000> but was:<8804>'); the gate's 14 atomic programs, three runs each at four threads, 42 PASS; the ladder's eight `atomic` programs `pass` with their recorded output. Meaning: Q2's shape (ii) is built; the cell path is unchanged in results.
4. **Under walk, an immutable array's second initialisation is now ignored, as a mutable array's is.** Before, `immutableArray[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3).fill(4)` held `4 4` (`PrimImmutableArray.java:73-82` at 157323e5 overwrote); after, `3 3`, since both arrays share the one store. Evidence: `tests/ArrayInitOnceWalk`, on the base 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 8 =/= a ZZ32: 6; an immutable array of ZZ32 filled twice', after 'OK'. Meaning: row 466 now covers both arrays and the compiled store.
5. **Under walk, the program's arguments are filled through the array's own `init`.** `StringPrim.GetProgramArgs` cast the varargs factory's result to the old glue's object (`StringPrim.java:135-141` at 157323e5); it now uses `IndexedArrayWrapper` (`:136-139`), as `NonPrimitive.java:243-247` fills varargs. Evidence: `ArrayStoreWalk`'s `SUM[\ZZ32\][a <- args] 1` equals `|args|`; the quick pair, which imports `System`, ALL PASS. Meaning: rung S's `args` replaces this path; until it lands, walk's `System` loads.
6. **The quick pair under walk on this branch: ALL PASS, 48 s and 42 s, under P-30's minute.** `explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh tmp/rung-array-store/mg rung-array-store`, 03:22:20 to 03:23:08 UTC, nproc 4, load 1.60: 'MicroGptAplQuick ... VERDICT: 7 PASS, 0 FAIL of 7 -- ALL PASS ... rc=0 secs=48', 'MicroGptFlatQuick ... rc=0 secs=42'. Meaning: the `cast` at each read keeps walk's check under a minute (fork A3).
7. **The distance stage's two crash rows in `value object Char` are gone on this branch's tree.** `distance/compare.sh`: 'DISTANCE SAME 0', 'crash gone decl ObjectDecl FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2 IllegalArgumentException Comparison method violates its general contract!', 'crash gone stage component FortressBuiltin leftover', 'crash new none'. Conditions: `Char` moved down 8 lines; row 929's sort is unrepaired, so they may come back on another tree. Meaning: declared nothing.

## For FACTS

**The one library's arrays hold their elements in a Java-backed store in a field, which walk answers with its own `AtomicArray`.** `NativeArray` is a plain component: `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` hold a `JavaArrayStore` of `FortressLibrary` in the field `mem` and read through `cast[\T\]`, `PrimImmutableRR64Array` a `JavaRR64ArrayStore`, now in the api with no factory choosing it (P-84, P-85). The stores' 7 bindings name `nativeHelpers/arrayOps` over the compiled `FortressArrayStore`, an `Object[]` whose elements the compiled transaction keys by array and index (`TXReadSlot`, `TXWriteSlot`), and `FortressRR64ArrayStore`, a `double[]`; NamingCzar's walk-world table reads the two classes as the two traits. Walk's loader answers each `arrayOps` name with `ArrayOps$<name>` over `FortressBuiltin`'s private `JavaArrayStoreObject`, an `AtomicArray`, and `JavaRR64ArrayStoreObject`, a `double[]`, and refuses a name with no operation at load. A second initialisation is ignored in both arrays and both stores (row 466). The count: 348 of the one library's 443 bindings name a helper, 95 a glue class (this branch). Tests: `tests/ArrayStoreWalk`, `ArrayStoreRR64Walk`, `ArrayInitOnceWalk`, `ArrayOpsMisspeltWalk`, `compiler/runtimeValues/ArrayStoreJUTest`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-array-store/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

Entries made false, for the record pass: F-299's 341 and 102, and its sentence that walk answers only `stringOps.typeName` and `equality.sEquiv` with its own operations (now also the seven of `arrayOps`, by a rule, not F-328's table); F-32's 102 (95 on this branch; the gather's merged count).

## Ledger changes

Row 466, its whole new line (the claim widened to the immutable array and the compiled store; reproducer `ArrayInitOnceWalk`; the notes cite the store's `init`), for `ledger.py rewrite 466`:

| 466 | **a second initialization of an array element is silently ignored, and the element keeps its first value**: under walk `a = array[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3); a.fill(4)` leaves `3 3`, and an immutable array's second fill too; the compiled store's `init` keeps the first value as well | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (prelude) | `Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/arrays-distributed.tex`, "Distributed Arrays" | `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayInitOnceWalk.fss` | climb batch 7 rung A | `PrimitiveArray.init0` and `PrimImmutableArray.init0` discard the `Boolean` of `init00`, the store's `init` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:21-24`, `:31-34`, at fe19fdad); the team's comment: validating it fails for an element initialized in a failed transaction. `AtomicArray.init` and `FortressArrayStore.init` store into an empty element only. The specification allows one initialization; its footnote and the api (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1510-1515`) say a duplicate signals an error. Fix: validate outside a transaction, or revise the footnote. Workaround: `a[i] := v`. full text: history, row 466 |

Row 527, its whole new line (walk no longer dies in the glue with `NegativeArraySizeException`; it stops at the store's factory, which takes a `ZZ32`), for `ledger.py rewrite 527`:

| 527 | under walk an array of a static size from 2^31 to 2^32-1 stops at its store's factory, where no catch sees it: `array1[\ZZ32, 3000000000\](7)` ends with 'Closure/Constructor for makeJavaArrayStore parameter 1 (n:ZZ32) got type Long' at `NativeArray.fss:16` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (prelude) | silent | none | climb batch 6.5b rung E | Such a size is a `ZZ64` value (row 418), and `PrimitiveArray`'s field passes `s0` to `makeJavaArrayStore(n: ZZ32)` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:16`, at fe19fdad), which takes no `ZZ64`; `PrimImmutableArray` and `PrimImmutableRR64Array` likewise (`:28`, `:38`). Fix: refuse a size above 2147483647 with a Fortress error naming it, the refusal P-40 places with the array design. No gated test can tell such a stop from a refusal. Probe `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-size-range/probes/skeptic/SkArraySize.fss`, in the parent of `ab067d9b6`. full text: history, row 527 |

Row 324, its whole new line (its notes' line citations of `Transaction.java` moved with the edit; the notes had 1 character left, so the first words of the mechanism are cut), for `ledger.py rewrite 324`:

| 324 | a Fortress exception thrown out of an `atomic` block leaves the block's writes visible on the compiled path: `atomic do g := 7; throw Boom end`, caught and read, gives 7 compiled and 100 under walk, at one thread and at four | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (codegen) | `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex`, "Atomic Expressions" | none | ours | Also for a local and an object. By reading, not measured: `CodeGen.forAtomicBlock` handles only `TransactionAbortException` (`CodeGen.java:1742-1745`), so an `FException` leaves without `BaseTask.cleanupTransaction`, and `Transaction.TXRead` returns an ancestral write (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:195-200,219-224`, at fe19fdad), which a later read finds; a second implicit thread reads it too (a child task takes its parent's transaction, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:83-86`). An `exit` to an enclosing `label` keeps the writes (`atomic.tex`). Workaround: throw before the block. probes and full text: history, row 324 |

New rows, for `ledger.py add`, in section 9 ("Arrays, vectors and matrices") and section 11 ("Parallelism, exceptions and control flow"):

| NEW-A-1 | under walk, a subscript out of the bounds of a `PrimitiveArray` or a `PrimImmutableArray` ends the run with a raw `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, which no catch sees: `array[\String\](2)[5]`, where a vector's subscript raises `FailCalled` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (prelude) | silent | none | climb batch 28 rung A | Their `opr [i:ZZ32]` and `opr [i:ZZ32] :=` call `get` and `put`, the api's unchecked indexing (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1520`), not `offset` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:17`, `:19`, `:29`, at fe19fdad), so the index reaches the store unchecked; `Array1`'s own subscript checks it in `offset` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2488-2492`). The api asks `i IN bounds()` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1395`). Fix: subscript through `offset(i)`. No gated test can pass while the run dies: `s = array[\String\](2).fill("x")` and `s[5]` in a `try` print 'ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 5 out of bounds for length 2', at 157323e5 and fe19fdad. |

| NEW-A-2 | on the compiled path, an `atomic` block that reads a variable that it wrote, then commits a nested `atomic` block and reads again, never ends: each attempt aborts at the second read and runs again | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (runtime) | `basic/expressions/atomic.tex`, "Atomic Expressions" | none | climb batch 28 rung A | A read of the transaction's own write records that write in the read set (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:220-224`, at fe19fdad); the nested commit moves the global clock (`:306`, `:346`), so the next read validates against the committed value (`:247`) and aborts, and each retry repeats it; array elements share the path. The compiled run step has no timeout (`tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:585`), so no gated test. `var x: ZZ32 = 0; var z: ZZ32 = 0` and `atomic do x := 2; y: ZZ32 = x; atomic do z := 1 end; w: ZZ32 = x end`, compiled, under `timeout 30`: exit 124 at 157323e5 and fe19fdad, one thread and four; without `y`, it ends. |

Each line above passes `explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py check --rows` (the two new rows checked with stand-in numbers; `NEW-A-1` and `NEW-A-2` fail only the number rule).

## Handover

Climb batch 28's rung A landed the arrays' store on `wip/rung-array-store`: `NativeArray` a plain component over `FortressLibrary`'s `JavaArrayStore` and `JavaRR64ArrayStore`, the 7 bindings on `nativeHelpers/arrayOps`, walk answering them with `ArrayOps` over an `AtomicArray`, the compiled `FortressArrayStore` over an `Object[]` tracked by the compiled transaction's new slot API; 348 helper and 95 glue bindings of 443 on the branch; count 0, distance 0 with row 929's crash rows gone; NEW-A-2, a compiled livelock of a transaction that reads its own write before a nested commit, recorded and not repaired (a reserved point).

## Revival change

**The change.**

- The team's `NativeArray` was a native component whose three objects were walk's native objects over glue classes: `native component NativeArray` and `get(i:ZZ32):T = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.PrimitiveArray$get")` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:12-50` at 157323e5), so walk alone could run an array. Tests: `tests/ArrayStoreWalk.fss`, `compiler/runtimeValues/ArrayStoreJUTest.java`. Reason: a body left on glue compiles to the library's own `builtinPrimitive`, whose body is `fail` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:34-35`), so every array, vector, varargs list and `args` of a compiled program would raise.
- The team's compiled transaction tracked only `MutableFValue` cells (`Hashtable<MutableFValue, Any> reads`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:27-28` at 157323e5). It now also tracks an element of an `Object[]` by its array and its index, `TXReadSlot` and `TXWriteSlot` (`Transaction.java:25-79`, `:203-231`, `:292-297`). Test: `ArrayStoreJUTest`, four tasks adding into one element inside `atomic`, exact. Reason: an array's elements have no cell each in an `Object[]` store, and a write inside `atomic` must be part of the transaction (`Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:68-75`).
- The team's walk store of an immutable array overwrote an element on a second initialisation (`interpreter/glue/prim/PrimImmutableArray.java:73-82` at 157323e5: `contents[i] = v; return (old == null)`), while a mutable array's ignored it (`AtomicArray.java:60-65`). Both arrays now share one store, and both ignore it: `immutableArray[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3).fill(4)` holds `3 3`. Test: `tests/ArrayInitOnceWalk.fss`. Reason: one store for both arrays; the api asks for one initialisation and an error on a second (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1510-1515`), which neither store signals.
- The team's `NativeArray` api declared `PrimitiveArray` and `PrimImmutableArray` only (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fsi:14-16` at 157323e5); it now also declares `PrimImmutableRR64Array` (`:18`), which a program can make; no factory chooses it. Test: `tests/ArrayStoreRR64Walk.fss`. Reason: base 'Function PrimImmutableRR64Array is not defined.'

**Provenance.** P-169 (the arrays' 7 on compiled helpers that walk's loader answers with its own operations, P-167's device; P-164's pattern of a Java-backed trait); the judgement's Q2, answered (ii), the slot API (review-queue item 407); the batch's forks A1 to A7 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:413-421`), A7 for the second initialisation; climb batch 28, rung A.

(* Under walk, the library's arrays of each rank, vectors, matrices, immutable arrays, lists, varargs and the program's arguments are made, written and read, a second fill keeps the first values, and parallel writes and atomic updates of one element are exact. *)
component ArrayStoreWalk
import NativeArray.{...}
import List.{...}
import System.{args}
export Executable

object Box(n: ZZ32) end

sumAll(xs: ZZ32...): ZZ32 = SUM[\ZZ32\][x <- xs] x

run(): () = do
    (* One dimension: a vector, and a PrimitiveArray of strings *)
    v = array[\ZZ32\](3).fill(7)
    v[1] := 8
    assert(v[0], 7, "vector element 0")
    assert(v[1], 8, "vector element 1")
    assert(|v|, 3, "vector size")
    s = array[\String\](3).fill("a")
    s[2] := "c"
    assert(s[0], "a", "string array element 0")
    assert(s[2], "c", "string array element 2")
    z: Array1[\String, 0, 3\] = PrimitiveArray[\String, 3\]()
    z.init(0, "cat")
    z.init(1, "dog")
    z.init(2, "bat")
    z[1] := "cow"
    assert(z[0], "cat", "PrimitiveArray element 0")
    assert(z.get(1), "cow", "PrimitiveArray element 1")
    b = array[\Box\](2).fill(Box(4))
    b[1] := Box(5)
    assert(b[0].n + b[1].n, 9, "array of objects")

    (* Two and three dimensions, and a matrix *)
    m = array[\ZZ32\](2, 3).fill(0)
    m[1, 2] := 5
    assert(m[1, 2], 5, "2-D element written")
    assert(m[0, 2], 0, "2-D element filled")
    c = array[\String\](2, 2, 2).fill("z")
    c[1, 0, 1] := "q"
    assert(c[1, 0, 1], "q", "3-D element written")
    assert(c[0, 1, 1], "z", "3-D element filled")
    mx = matrix[\ZZ32, 2, 2\]().fill(1)
    mx[0, 1] := 3
    assert(mx[0, 1] + mx[1, 1], 4, "matrix elements")
    tc = tabulatedArray1[\RR64, 4\](fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.5 i)
    assert(tc[3] = 1.5, "tabulated vector of RR64")

    (* Immutable arrays, frozen and thawed *)
    im = immutableArray[\ZZ32\](3).tabulate(fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 i)
    assert(im[2], 20, "immutable array element")
    pim: ImmutableArray1[\String, 0, 2\] = PrimImmutableArray[\String, 2\]()
    pim.init(0, "x")
    pim.init(1, "y")
    assert(pim[1], "y", "PrimImmutableArray element")
    fr = v.freeze()
    assert(fr[1], 8, "frozen vector")
    th = im.thaw()
    th[0] := 1
    assert(th[0] + th[2], 21, "thawed array")

    (* Lists, varargs and the program's arguments *)
    l = <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 2, 3|>
    l2 = l.addRight(4)
    assert(l2[3], 4, "list element")
    assert(|l2|, 4, "list size")
    assert(sumAll(1, 2, 3), 6, "varargs")
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][a <- args] 1, |args|, "program arguments")

    (* A second fill keeps the first values of a mutable array *)
    a = array[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3)
    a.fill(4)
    assert(a[0] + a[1], 6, "vector filled twice")
    t = array[\String\](2).fill("x")
    t.fill("y")
    assert(t[0] t[1], "xx", "string array filled twice")

    (* Parallel writes of distinct elements *)
    p = array[\ZZ32\](100).fill(0)
    for i <- 0#100 do p[i] := i end
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][i <- 0#100] p[i], 4950, "parallel writes to a vector")
    q = array[\Box\](50).fill(Box(0))
    for i <- 0#50 do q[i] := Box(i) end
    assert(SUM[\ZZ32\][i <- 0#50] q[i].n, 1225, "parallel writes to an array of objects")

    (* Atomic read-modify-writes of one element from a parallel loop *)
    acc = array[\ZZ32\](1).fill(0)
    for i <- 1#100 do atomic do acc[0] := acc[0] + i end end
    assert(acc[0], 5050, "atomic updates of a vector element")
    boxes = array[\Box\](1).fill(Box(0))
    for i <- 1#100 do atomic do boxes[0] := Box(boxes[0].n + i) end end
    assert(boxes[0].n, 5050, "atomic updates of an element of an array of objects")

    println("PASS")
end

end
(* Under walk, NativeArray's PrimImmutableRR64Array, made through its own constructor, reads back the RR64 values that it was initialised with. *)
component ArrayStoreRR64Walk
import NativeArray.{...}
export Executable

run(): () = do
    r = PrimImmutableRR64Array[\3\]()
    r.init0(0, 1.5)
    r.init0(1, 2.5)
    r.init0(2, 0.25)
    assert(r[0] + r[1] + r[2] = 4.25, "the sum of the elements")
    assert(r.get(1) = 2.5, "get")
    assert(|r|, 3, "size")
    w: ImmutableArray1[\RR64, 0, 2\] = PrimImmutableRR64Array[\2\]().fill(0.5)
    assert(w[0] + w[1] = 1.0, "filled")
    println("PASS")
end

end
(* Under walk, a second initialisation of an element keeps the element's first value, in a mutable array and in an immutable one. *)
component ArrayInitOnceWalk
import NativeArray.{...}
export Executable

run(): () = do
    a = array[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3)
    a.fill(4)
    assert(a[0] + a[1], 6, "a vector filled twice")
    s = array[\String\](2).fill("x")
    s.fill("y")
    assert(s[0] s[1], "xx", "an array of strings filled twice")
    im = immutableArray[\ZZ32\](2).fill(3)
    im.fill(4)
    assert(im[0] + im[1], 6, "an immutable array of ZZ32 filled twice")
    ims = immutableArray[\String\](2).fill("x")
    ims.fill("y")
    assert(ims[0] ims[1], "xx", "an immutable array of strings filled twice")
    p: ImmutableArray1[\String, 0, 1\] = PrimImmutableArray[\String, 1\]()
    p.init(0, "first")
    p.init(0, "second")
    assert(p[0], "first", "a PrimImmutableArray initialised twice")
    println("PASS")
end

end
(* Under walk, a builtinPrimitive string that names no helper of nativeHelpers.arrayOps is refused at load. *)
component ArrayOpsMisspeltWalk
export Executable

store(n: ZZ32): Any = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.arrayOps.makeStore")

run(): () = do
    _ = store(3)
    println("PASS")
end

end

285:1. **The natives come first** (P-33). V, R, H, A and S take bindings off glue classes: 50 of the 102, or 42 without A and Q3's half (below, "Where the natives stand").
286:2. **The reader rung can run now.** Climb batch 27's rung W declared both Java-backed traits and both table entries (F-330), so the reader rung builds on the base, not on another rung. It takes `FileWriteStream` too: an object of a native component cannot hold a field under walk (row 926), so `File` stops being native only when all its objects leave their glue together (item 373; PLAN item 69).
287:3. **The conversions no longer meet a rung of their batch.** Climb batch 27's rung I, which edited the same five integer traits, landed. Four of `IntLiteral`'s 8 (`asZZ32`, `asZZ64`, `asNN32`, `asNN64`) are written over `ZZ`'s checked getters, which V adds, and a rung cannot build on another rung of its own batch (PLAN, "The principle for the batches"); so the 8 sit in V, with their siblings (section 3, fork V2).
288:4. **S and T are climb batch 27's,** rebased: their files did not change in the lines they edit, and their walls reproduce on this base (section 5, probes 3 and 4).
289:5. **K makes the distance whole again.** Since climb batch 27 the distance does not check `value object Char`'s body, its 41 helper bindings among them (F-54). The prototype of K's linear extension removes both crash rows, checks `Char` with no error, keeps every other result, and takes 145 s against the base's 140 s for the distance and 88.9 s against 88.9 s for the count (probe 2). The brief records a rank sort at 299 s against 137 s.
290:6. **H and A both use P-167's device, at two places of walk's loader.** H adds six names to the table that rung A of climb batch 27 made (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:47-53`); A answers every name of its new helper class by one rule, where the loader reads the string (`:209`), about 150 lines apart (fork A4). So they merge.
291:7. **A and S's second half wait,** each on a question that is consequential by the `coordinator` skill's test (below). Without Q2's answer, A goes to climb batch 29; without Q3's, S builds its first half only.
292:8. **Seven rungs, each at its own declarations, keep the gather and the gate in bounds.** Section 4, "The rule the rungs keep", gives each rung's place in each shared file: four share `FortressBuiltin.fss`, four `FortressLibrary.fss` and three its api, each at other declarations. Climb batch 27 applied eight patches over the same two files with no conflict (`reviews/batch-27-review.md`, section 4).

387:1. **Seven rungs, V, R, A, K, H, S, T, in the manifest's order; none lands only with another; no two change one declaration.** Default: so. A leaves the manifest without Q2's answer, and S builds its first half without Q3's. The files that two rungs share, and each rung's place in each, are in section 4, "The rule the rungs keep, and how they meet". The gather orders the rungs that share a file by its own rule.
388:2. **The suites each rung runs, once, after its last change of code** (the `fortress-repo` skill's `tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). Default: V, R, A, H and S edit the library and a helper class that a binding names, and R, A and H walk too, so each runs `ant testSystem` and `ant testQuick` once, and its compiled guards through `junit.sh`; A also runs its compiled store's test at four threads. K edits the checker, so it runs `ant testQuick` once after its second pass (`compiler.md`, "The checker's time", step 4), and its compiled test through `junit.sh`. T edits the code generator only, so it runs its own tests through `junit.sh` and the harness and leaves the tracks to the gate, as climb batch 27's rung G did.
389:3. **Every rung but T runs the count stage and the distance stage once each, on its final tree, after its edit and rebuild.** Default: so; the before is climb batch 27's gate tables, the count 0 and the distance 0 with two crash rows (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/checker-count.txt` and `distance.txt`): run neither stage on the base. K runs the count stage three times by P-148 (base, change, pass) and the distance once on its final tree. (* Under walk, a second initialisation of an element keeps the element's first value, in a mutable array and in an immutable one. *)
component ArrayInitOnceWalk

export Executable

run(): () = do

    ims = immutableArray[\String\](2).fill("x")

end

#!/bin/bash
# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
DISTANCE SAME   0
    crash gone   decl	ObjectDecl FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2	IllegalArgumentException	Comparison method violates its general contract!
    crash gone   stage	component FortressBuiltin leftover	InterpreterBug	** bug! Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes. Component at FortressBuiltin.fss:12.1
    crash new    none

--- memory-model 68-75

\item Updates to shared mutable locations must always be performed using an
  \KWD{atomic} expression.  A location is considered to be shared if
  and only if that location can be accessed by more than one thread at
  a time.  For example, statically partitioning an array among many
  threads need not make the array elements shared; only elements
  actually accessed by more than one thread are considered to be
  shared.
--- 133-141
it performs additional computations.  Similarly, any subscripting
operation must be indistinguishable from accessing a single field.
Thus, accessor methods and subscripting methods should provide the
appearance of atomicity, as described in \secref{read-atomicity}.
\Library\ are written to preserve this abstraction.  For
example, the \TYP{Array} type in Fortress makes use of one or more
underlying \TYP{HeapSequence}s, and array subscripting
preserves the atomicity guarantees of this underlying object.
